BIOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Biology? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Biology.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Biology.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Biology.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Biology.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.

6. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

9. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Specimen Collection and Preservation? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Specimen Collection and Preservation.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Specimen Collection and Preservation.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Specimen Collection and Preservation.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Specimen Collection and Preservation.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Specimen Collection and Preservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Cell Structure and Specialisation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

2. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. A — newton (N)

4. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Biology.

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.

6. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

8. A — Ice melting to water

9. C — Producers

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
